what: Royal Gold buys royalties and streams on mines. It pays mining companies up front in exchange for a percentage of future production or revenue, so it earns from metal output without operating or building mines.
customers: Metal refiners and markets; its counterparties are the mining companies whose output it has rights to.
money: silver and copper interests, notably at Mount Milligan and Pueblo Viejo
moat: A portfolio of interests in large, long-life mines bought over decades, with no exposure to rising mining costs or capital overruns.
risks: Profit depends on gold and other metal prices
It has no control over how its partner mines are run
A low dividend yield of under 1%
Royalty acquisition competition has pushed prices up
opportunities: Operating margin of 62% and net margin of 45%, because it has almost no costs
Revenue grew about 43% last year and about 20% a year over three years
Almost no debt, so cash flow can fund new royalties
watch: Gold-equivalent ounces earned and new royalty acquisitions.
